title: Sep 16 Results + Sep 17 Preview: Eleven Wins and That Championship Feeling
summary: Our model crushed Sep 16 with an 11-4 record. Here's what clicked and tomorrow's top pick.

content.value:
## When the Model Gets Hot

Here's the thing about days like September 16th—they remind you why we trust the numbers. An 11-4 record with 73.3% accuracy isn't just good; it's the kind of day that makes you lean back in your chair and smile at the spreadsheet.

## The Hits That Connected

The Guardians pick at 61% confidence? Hit. The Giants squeaking by at just 51%? Still hit. That's seven straight correct calls before we even got to the night games. The Brewers delivered against Pittsburgh, the Phillies handled Washington, and the Orioles-Mets pick landed exactly where we thought it would.

The Cubs closing out the day with a win over the Braves was just the cherry on top.

## The Misses We Own

Let's talk about the Yankees and Dodgers picks. Both came in with solid confidence levels—54% and 61% respectively—and both missed. The Twins had other ideas in Minnesota, and the Reds played spoiler in Cincinnati.

But here's what matters: even our misses were reasonable calls. These weren't wild swings. They were calculated predictions that just didn't land. That's baseball.

## Tomorrow's Story: Back to Pittsburgh

And just like that, we're back where we won yesterday. The Milwaukee Brewers return to Pittsburgh on September 17th, and our model likes them again—this time at 52% confidence.

Kyle Harrison takes the mound for Milwaukee against Pittsburgh's Wilber Dotel. It's a tighter call than yesterday's 61% confidence, but the fundamentals are there. The Brewers showed us what they can do in this matchup, and we're riding that momentum into tomorrow.

## The Human Element

Days like September 16th don't come around all the time, and that's exactly why they matter. They're proof that when the model sees edges in the data, those edges are real. They translate to real games, real wins, real patterns.

But we're not getting ahead of ourselves. Tomorrow is a new slate. The Brewers-Pirates pick sits at 52%—basically a coin flip with a slight lean. We trust it, but we're also humble enough to know that 52% means we could just as easily be writing about a miss tomorrow.

That's the beauty of this whole thing. We show up, we analyze, we make the call, and then we watch it play out on the field. And on days like yesterday? We get to celebrate when it all clicks.

See you tomorrow for Sep 17's results. Let's see if Milwaukee can make it two in a row in Pittsburgh.
